# [AMD] Qwen3-Next: route GDN decode at AITER's fused gfx950 kernel

> **Requires AITER ≥ `dd6b8907`** — [ROCm/aiter#5520](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5520)
> (*[Triton/Gluon] Fused Qwen3-Next GDN decode op for gfx950*) **merged
> 2026-10-06** and added `fused_gdn_decode_qkvz` /
> `fused_gdn_decode_qkvz_supported` to `aiter.ops.triton.gated_delta_net`.
> This PR only consumes them.
>
> With the env var unset (the default) this PR does not import AITER at all.

## Motivation

Qwen3-Next's Gated DeltaNet decode step runs four kernels per layer, per step,
across 36 GDN layers:

```
fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat  ->  causal_conv1d_update
  ->  fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode  ->  gated RMSNorm
```

AITER ships a single Gluon kernel that does all four and consumes the packed
`qkvz`/`ba` projections directly. This wires Qwen3-Next to it.

**+4.7% to +8.6% output throughput** on 4x MI355X / TP4, no accuracy
regression. Off by default; opt in with
`SGLANG_QWEN3_NEXT_GDN_FUSED_BACKEND=aiter`.

Note the fused proj+Conv1D path that already exists in the GDN backend
(`fused_qkvzba_causal_conv1d_update_contiguous`) is **Qwen3.5-only** —
`_gdn_decode_fused_proj_conv` appears in `qwen3_5.py` and nowhere else — so
Qwen3-Next still runs the full unfused chain today.

## Modifications

The fusion spans SGLang's model/backend boundary, which is why this is not a
one-line dispatch change. `Qwen3GatedDeltaNet.forward` owns the qkvz split
(stage 1) and the gated RMSNorm (stage 5); `GDNAttnBackend.forward_decode` owns
the conv and recurrence (stages 2-4) and the state pools. Neither side holds all
the inputs: the backend receives post-split `mixed_qkv` and never sees `z` or
the norm weight, while the model never touches the mamba pools.

This follows the **attempt-and-verify stash** that Kimi-K3 already uses for its
fused KDA decode (`kimi_k3.py` / `kda_backend.py`): the model offers the
output-norm weight on the attention layer, the backend consumes it only if a
covered kernel engages, and the model applies its own norm when the stash comes
back unconsumed. Purely additive — no signature changes, and it fails safe.

New:
* `kernels/ops/attention/gdn_fused_decode_aiter.py` — fail-closed adapter:
  `enabled()` (env), `available()` (platform, AITER import, Triton Gluon),
  `covered()` (per-call contract) and `run()`. `covered()` delegates the tensor
  contract to AITER's own `fused_gdn_decode_qkvz_supported()` so the two cannot
  drift, and adds the one thing AITER cannot see — the model's output-gate
  activation, which the kernel hard-codes to SiLU.

* `test/srt/test_gdn_fused_decode_aiter.py` — the opt-in, the capability probe
  and every decline path. The decline cases need neither a GPU nor AITER, which
  is the point: they are exactly what CI can check on any runner.

Modified:
* `srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py` — `_try_aiter_fused_gdn_decode()`
  inside the existing `isinstance(mixed_qkv, tuple)` branch. Returns post-norm
  output and sets the consumed flag, or `None` to fall through to today's chain.
  Logs once on engage and once on reject-with-reason.
* `srt/models/qwen3_next.py` — the decode-only stash and fast path,
  `_gdn_fused_decode_ready` (static gate: platform, opt-in, head ratio, head
  dims, conv width), and `_prepare_gdn_fused_decode()` called from
  `load_weights` to publish the bf16 norm weight before graph capture. A zero
  conv bias is pre-allocated at init for models without one, so nothing is
  allocated inside a captured decode graph.

The backend's tuple input `(projected_qkvz, projected_ba)` already exists for
Qwen3.5's fused path; Qwen3-Next simply had not opted in. No new mechanism.

## Scope

**The CUDA path is unaffected.** The fused path requires `is_hip()` and gfx950,
and with the env var unset the probe returns `False` before AITER is imported,
leaving the existing chain byte-identical. Every gate degrades to the current
behaviour:

| gate | on failure |
|---|---|
| env var unset (default) | stock chain |
| not HIP / not gfx950 | stock chain |
| AITER or Triton Gluon unavailable | stock chain, logged once |
| Triton < 3.8 (see below) | stock chain, logged once with the reason |
| shape/dtype not covered | stock chain, logged once with the reason |
| output-gate activation is not SiLU | stock chain |

Following `_can_fuse_accept_state`'s framing in `kda_backend.py`: this is a
capability, not a mode — falling short of the contract falls back rather than
raising.

SGLang authors no Gluon; this only *consumes* AITER's, and Gluon availability is
probed rather than pinned, as `aiter_mla_gluon.py` does.

### A note on Triton 3.7 images

Some ROCm builds ship Triton **3.7** carrying a backported Gluon that *imports
cleanly* but miscompiles the layout ops this kernel uses. AITER therefore gates
on `triton >= 3.8` rather than on an import probe. On such an image this feature
declines and falls back — correct, but inert. Concretely, of the 2026-10-12
nightlies, `rocm724` ships Triton 3.7.0 and `rocm10` ships 3.8.0.

## Environment

Hardware: 4x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), TP4 / EP1.
Image: `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261012`.
Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8`.

| component | version | note |
|---|---|---|
| sglang | 2026-10-12 | matches main at time of testing |
| Triton | **3.8.0** | native — no manual install needed on this image |
| AITER | 2026-09-25 in-image | predates #5520; install AITER ≥ `dd6b8907` |

Both arms differ by **exactly this PR's commits** — the baseline is this
branch's own merge base (`f92199b569`), not an older image default, so no
unrelated upstream drift is folded into the comparison. Random dataset,
ISL/OSL 1024/1024, `--random-range-ratio 1`,
`num-prompts == max-concurrency`. All numbers **un-profiled**.

## Accuracy Tests

`python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319 --parallel 256`
(the old `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py` has been removed from main):

| | decode cap 64 | decode cap 256 |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 0.943 | 0.940 |
| this PR | **0.946** | **0.942** |
| Invalid (both arms) | 0.000 | 0.000 |

Standard error at n=1319, p~0.94 is 0.0065, so this is "no detected
regression" rather than a measured equality. **One run per arm per
configuration.**

Kernel-level correctness lives in the AITER PR: the op is verified
**bit-identical** to its reference implementation on all five outputs across
batch 1-256, and its test suite covers the pad-slot contract, every dispatch
branch and determinism.

## Speed Tests

| conc | baseline tok/s | this PR tok/s | delta | baseline TPOT | this PR TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 368.20 | 391.42 | **+6.3%** | 5.36 ms | 5.04 ms |
| 8 | 2712.32 | 2850.68 | **+5.1%** | 5.75 ms | 5.47 ms |
| 32 | 8301.50 | 8987.28 | **+8.3%** | 7.40 ms | 6.82 ms |
| 64 | 13240.56 | 14377.92 | **+8.6%** | 9.20 ms | 8.43 ms |

Engagement is confirmed structurally from the server log — one
`AITER fused GDN decode engaged` line and **zero** `not covered` lines — so the
throughput above is attributable to the fused path actually running, not to a
silent fallback.

### Raised graph cap

AITER's op carries a second decomposition above batch 128, which only fires when
`--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` exceeds its default of 64. Same two arms at a cap
of 256:

| conc | baseline tok/s | this PR tok/s | delta | baseline TPOT | this PR TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 21701.42 | 22863.24 | **+5.4%** | 11.05 ms | 10.44 ms |
| 256 | 31343.49 | 32821.80 | **+4.7%** | 14.98 ms | 14.25 ms |

The gain narrows at the top of the range, as expected — the decode kernel is a
smaller share of step time once the batch is large enough to be bandwidth-bound.

At this cap SGLang captures **36** decode graph sizes and the op covers all of
them; selection inside AITER is a range check, not a shape table.

### Kernel level

Per decode step, 36 GDN layers, TP-0, from torch profiler traces. **These traces
were taken on the earlier ROCm 7.0 image and have not been re-collected on the
image above** — the ratio is the claim, not the absolute microseconds:

| kernel | baseline | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode_kernel` | 36x, 361.6 us | **0** |
| `fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat_kernel` | 36x, 163.5 us | **0** |
| `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` | 36x, 155.7 us | **0** |
| `layer_norm_gated_fwd_kernel` | 36x, 149.9 us | **0** |
| AITER fused GDN decode | 0 | **36x, 279.2 us** |
| **total** | **830.8 us** | **279.2 us (2.98x)** |

### Methodology notes

Both arms were run with an idle-GPU assertion (no server processes, <3% VRAM)
before each arm, not just between them. An earlier ladder produced a spurious
-80% baseline result from contention with a stale server; it reproduced within
that session, which is precisely why the guard now runs per arm.

Absolute throughput here is **not comparable** to the figures previously quoted
in this PR: those came from a ROCm 7.0 image with Triton 3.8 installed manually,
these from ROCm 10 with native 3.8 — a different compiler and a different
absolute scale. The arm-vs-arm deltas are the like-for-like comparison, and they
are unchanged across that move and a ~1700-commit jump in main.

## Known gaps

* **The FP8 epilogue is not wired up.** The AITER op can emit per-head group-128
  FP8 activations that a block-FP8 `out_proj` consumes directly, removing a
  further `dynamic_per_group_scaled_quant` launch per GDN layer. This PR calls
  it with `quant_dtype=None`. Measured against an out-of-tree reference
  implementation that does use it, that leaves roughly **2 percentage points**
  of throughput on the table. It is deferred because no linear-attention backend
  currently returns an `(fp8, scales)` tuple into a `Linear`, and it deserves its
  own gate and its own review.

## Reproduction

```bash
docker run --rm -it --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --network host \
  --group-add video --ipc host --shm-size 32g \
  -v $HF_HOME:/hf lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261012

# The image's AITER predates #5520; install one that contains it.
pip install -U "git+https://github.com/ROCm/aiter.git@main"   # >= dd6b8907

export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1
export SGLANG_QWEN3_NEXT_GDN_FUSED_BACKEND=aiter   # omit for the baseline arm

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --ep-size 1 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --quantization fp8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --attention-backend aiter --moe-runner-backend aiter \
  --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion \
  --disable-radix-cache --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --context-length 8192 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --port 8888 --trust-remote-code
```

## Checklist

- [x] Off by default; unconditional fallback to the existing chain
- [x] `pre-commit` clean on all changed files
- [x] DCO sign-off on every commit
- [x] CUDA path explicitly unaffected (see Scope)
- [x] Registered test (`test/srt/test_gdn_fused_decode_aiter.py`, 9 tests)
- [x] Companion AITER PR merged (`dd6b8907`) and the minimum version stated
- [ ] 3x GSM8K per arm

Rebased onto current main and refreshed every number. Description updated with the full tables; summary of what changed:

**Conflict resolved.** Merged `main` — no force-push, commit history preserved. The one conflict was in `gdn_backend.py`: upstream added target-verify qkv routing helpers at the same point in `GDNAttnBackend` where this PR adds `_try_aiter_fused_gdn_decode`. Both kept, since the additions are independent.

**The AITER dependency is no longer pending.** ROCm/aiter#5520 merged on 2026-10-06 (`dd6b8907`), so the description now pins a concrete minimum version instead of referencing an open PR.

@yichiche — on your earlier note about guarding the NVIDIA path: that is addressed in `40a88fd19e`. `_use_aiter = get_bool_env_var("SGLANG_USE_AITER") and is_hip()` now gates both the forward-path branch and the constructor's readiness check. I used `_use_aiter` rather than `is_hip` per your guidance, since the kernel imports from AITER. With the flag unset nothing is probed, allocated or dispatched.

**Re-validated end to end** on a current nightly (`lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261012`, sglang 2026-10-12). Both arms on the same image in the same session, differing by exactly this PR's commits — the baseline is this branch's own merge base rather than an older image default, so no unrelated upstream drift is folded in.

| concurrency | 1 | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128¹ | 256¹ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| throughput delta | +6.3% | +5.1% | +8.3% | +8.6% | +5.4% | +4.7% |

¹ with `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256`, which is what enables AITER's large-batch decomposition.

GSM8K (1319 questions): **0.943 → 0.946** at the default cap and **0.940 → 0.942** at the raised cap, `Invalid: 0.000` in all four runs. The fused path logs its engage line exactly once per server with zero `not covered` fallbacks, so the measured arm really is running the kernel rather than quietly falling back.

These deltas are within a point of what this PR originally claimed, now carried across a ~1700-commit jump in main, a merged AITER dependency, and a move to ROCm 10 with native Triton 3.8.

Two things worth flagging for reviewers:

- **Absolute throughput is not comparable to the figures previously in this PR.** Those came from a ROCm 7.0 image with Triton 3.8 installed manually; these come from ROCm 10 with native 3.8 — different compiler, different absolute scale. The arm-vs-arm deltas are the like-for-like comparison.
- **On Triton 3.7 images this feature is inert.** Some ROCm builds ship a backported Gluon that imports cleanly but miscompiles the layout ops this kernel uses, so AITER gates on `triton >= 3.8` rather than on an import probe. On those images the path declines and falls back cleanly rather than failing. Of the 2026-10-12 nightlies, `rocm724` ships 3.7.0 and `rocm10` ships 3.8.0.

The reproduction block in the description also gained three flags that were used for every measurement but had never been published (`--disable-radix-cache`, `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.80`), and the GSM8K command changed, since `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py` no longer exists in main — it is `python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k` now.

Ready for another look.

@yichiche **The registered test was not actually reaching CI, and now is.** (addressed in commit [5d220d9](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39554/commits/5d220d90846f6cd78debefa0b417909eedd9c120)) It had been added under `test/srt/`, which `run_suite.py` no longer discovers — collection globs `test/registered/**/*.py`, and `test/srt` is referenced by no workflow. The directory is down to four pre-migration files against ~2260 under `test/registered/`, so nothing collected ours and the suite silently never ran it. Moved to `test/registered/attention/` alongside the other GDN and KDA attention tests, with the registration marker discovery requires (the glob is strict, so a file placed there without one fails collection rather than being skipped). Registered for `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`: the op is gfx950-only, so that is the suite where the device-dependent class runs instead of skipping, and there is no CUDA registration because the fused path is unreachable off ROCm. Verified via `collect_tests(..., sanity_check=True)` that it is now picked up, and the 9 tests pass from the new path.

Image: `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261012`.
Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8`.

| component | version | note |
|---|---|---|
| sglang | 2026-10-12 | matches main at time of testing |
| Triton | **3.8.0** | native — no manual install needed on this image |
| AITER | 2026-09-25 in-image | predates #5520; install AITER ≥ `dd6b8907` |

Both arms differ by **exactly this PR's commits** — the baseline is this
branch's own merge base (`f92199b569`), not an older image default, so no
unrelated upstream drift is folded into the comparison. Random dataset,
ISL/OSL 1024/1024, `--random-range-ratio 1`,
`num-prompts == max-concurrency`. All numbers **un-profiled**.

## Accuracy Tests

`python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319 --parallel 256`
(the old `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py` has been removed from main):

| | decode cap 64 | decode cap 256 |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 0.943 | 0.940 |
| this PR | **0.946** | **0.942** |
| Invalid (both arms) | 0.000 | 0.000 |

Standard error at n=1319, p~0.94 is 0.0065, so this is "no detected
regression" rather than a measured equality. **One run per arm per
configuration.**

Kernel-level correctness lives in the AITER PR: the op is verified
**bit-identical** to its reference implementation on all five outputs across
batch 1-256, and its test suite covers the pad-slot contract, every dispatch
branch and determinism.

## Speed Tests

| conc | baseline tok/s | this PR tok/s | delta | baseline TPOT | this PR TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 368.20 | 391.42 | **+6.3%** | 5.36 ms | 5.04 ms |
| 8 | 2712.32 | 2850.68 | **+5.1%** | 5.75 ms | 5.47 ms |
| 32 | 8301.50 | 8987.28 | **+8.3%** | 7.40 ms | 6.82 ms |
| 64 | 13240.56 | 14377.92 | **+8.6%** | 9.20 ms | 8.43 ms |

Engagement is confirmed structurally from the server log — one
`AITER fused GDN decode engaged` line and **zero** `not covered` lines — so the
throughput above is attributable to the fused path actually running, not to a
silent fallback.

### Raised graph cap

AITER's op carries a second decomposition above batch 128, which only fires when
`--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` exceeds its default of 64. Same two arms at a cap
of 256:

| conc | baseline tok/s | this PR tok/s | delta | baseline TPOT | this PR TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 21701.42 | 22863.24 | **+5.4%** | 11.05 ms | 10.44 ms |
| 256 | 31343.49 | 32821.80 | **+4.7%** | 14.98 ms | 14.25 ms |

The gain narrows at the top of the range, as expected — the decode kernel is a
smaller share of step time once the batch is large enough to be bandwidth-bound.

At this cap SGLang captures **36** decode graph sizes and the op covers all of
them; selection inside AITER is a range check, not a shape table.

### Kernel level

Per decode step, 36 GDN layers, TP-0, from torch profiler traces. **These traces
were taken on the earlier ROCm 7.0 image and have not been re-collected on the
image above** — the ratio is the claim, not the absolute microseconds:

| kernel | baseline | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode_kernel` | 36x, 361.6 us | **0** |
| `fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat_kernel` | 36x, 163.5 us | **0** |
| `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` | 36x, 155.7 us | **0** |
| `layer_norm_gated_fwd_kernel` | 36x, 149.9 us | **0** |
| AITER fused GDN decode | 0 | **36x, 279.2 us** |
| **total** | **830.8 us** | **279.2 us (2.98x)** |

### Methodology notes

Both arms were run with an idle-GPU assertion (no server processes, <3% VRAM)
before each arm, not just between them. An earlier ladder produced a spurious
-80% baseline result from contention with a stale server; it reproduced within
that session, which is precisely why the guard now runs per arm.

Absolute throughput here is **not comparable** to the figures previously quoted
in this PR: those came from a ROCm 7.0 image with Triton 3.8 installed manually,
these from ROCm 10 with native 3.8 — a different compiler and a different
absolute scale. The arm-vs-arm deltas are the like-for-like comparison, and they
are unchanged across that move and a ~1700-commit jump in main.

## Known gaps

* **The FP8 epilogue is not wired up.** The AITER op can emit per-head group-128
  FP8 activations that a block-FP8 `out_proj` consumes directly, removing a
  further `dynamic_per_group_scaled_quant` launch per GDN layer. This PR calls
  it with `quant_dtype=None`. Measured against an out-of-tree reference
  implementation that does use it, that leaves roughly **2 percentage points**
  of throughput on the table. It is deferred because no linear-attention backend
  currently returns an `(fp8, scales)` tuple into a `Linear`, and it deserves its
  own gate and its own review.

## Reproduction

```bash
docker run --rm -it --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --network host \
  --group-add video --ipc host --shm-size 32g \
  -v $HF_HOME:/hf lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261012

# The image's AITER predates #5520; install one that contains it.
pip install -U "git+https://github.com/ROCm/aiter.git@main"   # >= dd6b8907

export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1
export SGLANG_QWEN3_NEXT_GDN_FUSED_BACKEND=aiter   # omit for the baseline arm

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --ep-size 1 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --quantization fp8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --attention-backend aiter --moe-runner-backend aiter \
  --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion \
  --disable-radix-cache --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --context-length 8192 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --port 8888 --trust-remote-code
```

## Checklist

- [x] Off by default; unconditional fallback to the existing chain
- [x] `pre-commit` clean on all changed files
- [x] DCO sign-off on every commit
- [x] CUDA path explicitly unaffected (see Scope)
- [x] Registered test (`test/srt/test_gdn_fused_decode_aiter.py`, 9 tests)
- [x] Companion AITER PR merged (`dd6b8907`) and the minimum version stated
- [ ] 3x GSM8K per arm

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Fail-closed adapter for AITER's gfx950 fused Qwen3-Next GDN decode.
+
+One AITER Gluon launch replaces the four-kernel decode chain
+``fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat -> causal_conv1d_update ->
+fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode -> gated RMSNorm``, folding the
+output gated RMSNorm into the recurrence kernel. The gate reaches the kernel via
+the attempt-and-verify stash on the attention layer (see qwen3_next.py), the
+same handoff Kimi-K3 uses for its fused KDA decode.
+
+Everything is probed, nothing is assumed: platform, opt-in env var, AITER import,
+and a per-call ``covered()`` shape/dtype contract. Any miss leaves the stash
+unconsumed and the caller runs the ordinary unfused chain.
+
+SGLang authors no Gluon; this only consumes AITER's, and Triton/Gluon
+availability is probed rather than pinned.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import os
+from typing import Optional, Tuple
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_hip
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+_HEAD_DIM = 128
+_CONV_WIDTH = 4
+
+
+def enabled() -> bool:
+    """Opt-in. Off by default, like the other fused-decode backends."""
+    return os.environ.get("SGLANG_QWEN3_NEXT_GDN_FUSED_BACKEND", "").lower() == "aiter"
+
+
+def _ops():
+    try:
+        from aiter.ops.triton.gated_delta_net.fused_gdn_decode_qkvz import (
+            fused_gdn_decode_qkvz,
+            fused_gdn_decode_qkvz_supported,
+        )
+    except (ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError) as exc:
+        logger.debug("aiter fused GDN decode import failed: %s", exc)
+        return None, None
+    return fused_gdn_decode_qkvz, fused_gdn_decode_qkvz_supported
+
+
+def available() -> bool:
+    """Platform, opt-in, import, and Gluon toolchain, in that order."""
+    if not is_hip() or not enabled() or not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        return False
+    run, _ = _ops()
+    if run is None:
+        return False
+    try:
+        # The AITER kernel is Gluon. Probe the module AND the one arch-specific
+        # primitive it needs: a Triton that has `experimental.gluon` but not
+        # `gl.amd.cdna3` would import cleanly and then fail at first kernel
+        # compile with an opaque error, which is exactly the failure this gate
+        # exists to prevent. SGLang does not pin Triton, so feature-probe rather
+        # than version-compare.
+        import triton.experimental.gluon.language as gl
+
+        if not hasattr(getattr(getattr(gl, "amd", None), "cdna3", None), "buffer_load"):
+            logger.info(
+                "aiter fused GDN decode disabled: Triton Gluon lacks "
+                "gl.amd.cdna3.buffer_load"
+            )
+            return False
+    except ImportError as exc:
+        logger.info("aiter fused GDN decode disabled, no Triton Gluon: %s", exc)
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def covered(
+    projected_qkvz: torch.Tensor,
+    projected_ba: torch.Tensor,
+    conv_state: torch.Tensor,
+    ssm_state: torch.Tensor,
+    state_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    conv_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    conv_bias: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    A_log: torch.Tensor,
+    dt_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    activation: Optional[str],
+    quant_dtype: Optional[torch.dtype],
+) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
+    """Per-call contract check. Returns ``(covered, reason)``.
+
+    Delegates the tensor contract to AITER's own predicate so the two cannot
+    drift, and adds the one thing AITER cannot see: the model's output-gate
+    activation, which the kernel hard-codes to SiLU.
+    """
+    if activation not in ("silu", "swish"):
+        return False, f"kernel fuses a SiLU output gate, model uses {activation!r}"
+    if conv_bias is None:
+        return False, "conv bias is required"
+    _, supported = _ops()
+    if supported is None:
+        return False, "aiter fused GDN decode unavailable"
+    return supported(
+        projected_qkvz,
+        projected_ba,
+        conv_state,
+        ssm_state,
+        state_indices,
+        conv_weight,
+        conv_bias,
+        A_log,
+        dt_bias,
+        norm_weight,
+        quant_dtype,
+    )
+
+
+def run(
+    *,
+    projected_qkvz: torch.Tensor,
+    projected_ba: torch.Tensor,
+    conv_state: torch.Tensor,
+    ssm_state: torch.Tensor,
+    state_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    conv_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    conv_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    A_log: torch.Tensor,
+    dt_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    scale: float,
+    norm_eps: float,
+    pad_slot_id: int,
+    quant_dtype: Optional[torch.dtype] = None,
+):
+    """Run the fused decode. Mutates ``conv_state`` and ``ssm_state`` in place.
+
+    Returns ``(out, quantized, scales)``; the latter two are ``None`` unless
+    ``quant_dtype`` is given.
+    """
+    run_fn, _ = _ops()
+    return run_fn(
+        projected_qkvz,
+        projected_ba,
+        conv_state,
+        ssm_state,
+        state_indices,
+        conv_weight,
+        conv_bias,
+        A_log,
+        dt_bias,
+        norm_weight,
+        scale=scale,
+        norm_eps=norm_eps,
+        quant_dtype=quant_dtype,
+        pad_slot_id=pad_slot_id,
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Tests for the AITER fused Qwen3-Next GDN decode integration.
+
+The integration is a capability, not a mode: every gate must degrade to the
+existing unfused chain rather than raise. These tests pin that, and they pin it
+without needing a GPU or AITER for the cases that matter most -- the ones where
+the fused path must decline.
+
+The kernel's numerics are covered in AITER's own op tests; what is tested here
+is SGLang's side of the contract: the probe, the fallback, and the
+attempt-and-verify stash.
+"""
+
+import os
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention import gdn_fused_decode_aiter as adapter
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+# AMD only. The op under test is gfx950, so mi35x is the suite where the
+# device-dependent class runs rather than skips. No register_cuda_ci: the fused
+# path is unreachable off ROCm by construction.
+register_amd_ci(est_time=10, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x")
+
+_ENV = "SGLANG_QWEN3_NEXT_GDN_FUSED_BACKEND"
+
+
+class TestGdnFusedDecodeAiterGating(CustomTestCase):
+    """The opt-in and the capability probe."""
+
+    def test_disabled_by_default(self):
+        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {}, clear=False):
+            os.environ.pop(_ENV, None)
+            self.assertFalse(adapter.enabled())
+            self.assertFalse(adapter.available())
+
+    def test_enabled_only_for_aiter_value(self):
+        for value, expected in (
+            ("aiter", True),
+            ("AITER", True),
+            ("triton", False),
+            ("", False),
+            ("1", False),
+        ):
+            with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {_ENV: value}):
+                self.assertEqual(adapter.enabled(), expected, f"value={value!r}")
+
+    def test_unavailable_when_not_hip(self):
+        with (
+            mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {_ENV: "aiter"}),
+            mock.patch.object(adapter, "is_hip", return_value=False),
+        ):
+            self.assertFalse(adapter.available())
+
+    def test_unavailable_when_aiter_missing(self):
+        with (
+            mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {_ENV: "aiter"}),
+            mock.patch.object(adapter, "_ops", return_value=(None, None)),
+        ):
+            self.assertFalse(adapter.available())
+
+
+class TestGdnFusedDecodeAiterCoverage(CustomTestCase):
+    """covered() must decline, with a reason, rather than raise."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _args(**over):
+        base = dict(
+            projected_qkvz=torch.empty(0),
+            projected_ba=torch.empty(0),
+            conv_state=torch.empty(0),
+            ssm_state=torch.empty(0),
+            state_indices=torch.empty(0),
+            conv_weight=torch.empty(0),
+            conv_bias=torch.empty(0),
+            A_log=torch.empty(0),
+            dt_bias=torch.empty(0),
+            norm_weight=torch.empty(0),
+            activation="silu",
+            quant_dtype=None,
+        )
+        base.update(over)
+        return base
+
+    def test_declines_non_silu_activation(self):
+        """The kernel folds a SiLU output gate; anything else is wrong numerics.
+
+        This is the one condition AITER's predicate cannot see, so it must be
+        checked on the SGLang side.
+        """
+        for activation in ("gelu", "relu", None):
+            ok, reason = adapter.covered(**self._args(activation=activation))
+            self.assertFalse(ok, f"activation={activation!r} must decline")
+            self.assertIn("SiLU", reason)
+
+    def test_declines_without_conv_bias(self):
+        ok, reason = adapter.covered(**self._args(conv_bias=None))
+        self.assertFalse(ok)
+        self.assertIn("bias", reason.lower())
+
+    def test_declines_when_aiter_unavailable(self):
+        with mock.patch.object(adapter, "_ops", return_value=(None, None)):
+            ok, reason = adapter.covered(**self._args())
+            self.assertFalse(ok)
+            self.assertTrue(reason)
+
+    def test_reason_is_non_empty_on_every_decline(self):
+        """A decline is logged once by the caller; an empty reason is useless."""
+        ok, reason = adapter.covered(**self._args(activation="gelu"))
+        self.assertFalse(ok)
+        self.assertTrue(reason.strip())
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.version.hip, "requires a ROCm GPU"
+)
+class TestGdnFusedDecodeAiterOnDevice(CustomTestCase):
+    """Contract checks that need a device. Skipped off ROCm, and off gfx950."""
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        # The probe is opt-in, so enable it for the duration of this test rather
+        # than requiring the suite to be run with the env var already set.
+        self._env = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {_ENV: "aiter"})
+        self._env.start()
+        self.addCleanup(self._env.stop)
+        if not adapter.available():
+            self.skipTest("aiter fused GDN decode not available here")
+
+    def test_declines_wrong_head_ratio(self):
+        """num_v_heads must be 2 * num_k_heads; the kernel static_asserts it."""
+        dev, kh, vh, d = "cuda", 4, 4, 128  # vh == kh, not 2*kh
+        channels = 2 * kh * d + vh * d
+        ok, reason = adapter.covered(
+            projected_qkvz=torch.zeros(8, kh * 768, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev),
+            projected_ba=torch.zeros(8, 2 * vh, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev),
+            conv_state=torch.zeros(16, channels, 3, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev),
+            ssm_state=torch.zeros(16, vh, d, d, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev),
+            state_indices=torch.arange(1, 9, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev),
+            conv_weight=torch.zeros(channels, 4, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev),
+            conv_bias=torch.zeros(channels, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev),
+            A_log=torch.zeros(vh, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev),
+            dt_bias=torch.zeros(vh, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev),
+            norm_weight=torch.zeros(d, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev),
+            activation="silu",
+            quant_dtype=None,
+        )
+        self.assertFalse(ok)
+        self.assertTrue(reason)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

issue_comments.body:
Rebased onto current main and refreshed every number. Description updated with the full tables; summary of what changed:

**Conflict resolved.** Merged `main` — no force-push, commit history preserved. The one conflict was in `gdn_backend.py`: upstream added target-verify qkv routing helpers at the same point in `GDNAttnBackend` where this PR adds `_try_aiter_fused_gdn_decode`. Both kept, since the additions are independent.

**The AITER dependency is no longer pending.** ROCm/aiter#5520 merged on 2026-10-06 (`dd6b8907`), so the description now pins a concrete minimum version instead of referencing an open PR.

@yichiche — on your earlier note about guarding the NVIDIA path: that is addressed in `40a88fd19e`. `_use_aiter = get_bool_env_var("SGLANG_USE_AITER") and is_hip()` now gates both the forward-path branch and the constructor's readiness check. I used `_use_aiter` rather than `is_hip` per your guidance, since the kernel imports from AITER. With the flag unset nothing is probed, allocated or dispatched.

**Re-validated end to end** on a current nightly (`lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261012`, sglang 2026-10-12). Both arms on the same image in the same session, differing by exactly this PR's commits — the baseline is this branch's own merge base rather than an older image default, so no unrelated upstream drift is folded in.

| concurrency | 1 | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128¹ | 256¹ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| throughput delta | +6.3% | +5.1% | +8.3% | +8.6% | +5.4% | +4.7% |

¹ with `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256`, which is what enables AITER's large-batch decomposition.

GSM8K (1319 questions): **0.943 → 0.946** at the default cap and **0.940 → 0.942** at the raised cap, `Invalid: 0.000` in all four runs. The fused path logs its engage line exactly once per server with zero `not covered` fallbacks, so the measured arm really is running the kernel rather than quietly falling back.

These deltas are within a point of what this PR originally claimed, now carried across a ~1700-commit jump in main, a merged AITER dependency, and a move to ROCm 10 with native Triton 3.8.

Two things worth flagging for reviewers:

- **Absolute throughput is not comparable to the figures previously in this PR.** Those came from a ROCm 7.0 image with Triton 3.8 installed manually; these come from ROCm 10 with native 3.8 — different compiler, different absolute scale. The arm-vs-arm deltas are the like-for-like comparison.
- **On Triton 3.7 images this feature is inert.** Some ROCm builds ship a backported Gluon that imports cleanly but miscompiles the layout ops this kernel uses, so AITER gates on `triton >= 3.8` rather than on an import probe. On those images the path declines and falls back cleanly rather than failing. Of the 2026-10-12 nightlies, `rocm724` ships 3.7.0 and `rocm10` ships 3.8.0.

The reproduction block in the description also gained three flags that were used for every measurement but had never been published (`--disable-radix-cache`, `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.80`), and the GSM8K command changed, since `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py` no longer exists in main — it is `python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k` now.

Ready for another look.

@yichiche **The registered test was not actually reaching CI, and now is.** (addressed in commit [5d220d9](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39554/commits/5d220d90846f6cd78debefa0b417909eedd9c120)) It had been added under `test/srt/`, which `run_suite.py` no longer discovers — collection globs `test/registered/**/*.py`, and `test/srt` is referenced by no workflow. The directory is down to four pre-migration files against ~2260 under `test/registered/`, so nothing collected ours and the suite silently never ran it. Moved to `test/registered/attention/` alongside the other GDN and KDA attention tests, with the registration marker discovery requires (the glob is strict, so a file placed there without one fails collection rather than being skipped). Registered for `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`: the op is gfx950-only, so that is the suite where the device-dependent class runs instead of skipping, and there is no CUDA registration because the fused path is unreachable off ROCm. Verified via `collect_tests(..., sanity_check=True)` that it is now picked up, and the 9 tests pass from the new path.
